title: He ran ahead.
paragraphs: He ran ahead.
That’s the part that hit me.

Not the money.
Not the reputation.
Not even the fact that Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector with a name people probably spat out in disgust.

It was this:
He climbed a tree just to see Jesus.
“So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see him, since Jesus was coming that way.” — Luke 19:4
And the lesson broke me.
Sometimes the greatest miracle starts when pride finally loses its grip.

Zacchaeus was a grown man.
Rich.
Powerful.
Important in the eyes of the world.

But when Jesus passed by, none of that could help him get close.
His status could not lift him.
His money could not clear the crowd.
His title could not open heaven.
So he did something undignified.
He climbed.

That’s the lesson I learned:
You will never truly see Jesus until you stop protecting your image more than your soul.

Zacchaeus didn’t care how foolish he looked.
He was desperate.
Hungry.
Ready.
And that kind of hunger always gets heaven’s attention.
But here’s what we miss:

Zacchaeus thought he was the one searching for Jesus.
In reality, Jesus was already coming for him.

That is the Gospel.
We climb in our weakness, but Christ comes in His mercy.
We reach, but He saves.
We make a small move of faith, and He calls us by name.

“Zacchaeus, come down immediately. I must stay at your house today.”
Jesus did not merely notice a sinner in a tree.
He invited Himself into the life of a broken man.
And everything changed.

Conviction came.
Repentance came.
Restoration came.

Because real encounters with Jesus do not leave us cute.
They leave us changed.

So here is the lesson:
Climb whatever pride tells you not to climb.
Leave behind the dignity that keeps you distant from Christ.
Pray the prayer.
Open the Bible.
Go to church.
Repent honestly.
Cry if you need to.
Run ahead of the crowd if you must.
Just don’t let your ego keep you on the ground.

The tree was awkward.
But it became the place of encounter.

And maybe that’s your word today:
The very place that feels embarrassing may become the place where Jesus calls your name.

There is hope for the curious.
Hope for the ashamed.
Hope for the compromised.
Hope for the one everyone has already labeled.

Jesus still stops.
Jesus still looks up.
Jesus still calls sinners down.
Jesus still enters houses people think are too dirty for Him.
